title: Investigate spotty host client connection rendering
Inspect repository architecture for host-client rendering and transport behavior
Summarize spotty-connection rendering behavior for the user

content: Started inspecting the repository for code that defines host/client transport, render scheduling, and missed-frame behavior.

observation: The host exposes both live WebSocket events at /ws and recovery-oriented HTTP APIs for session snapshots and event replay via /api/sessions/:id/snapshot and /api/sessions/:id/events?since=N.

The mobile HostClient currently opens a WebSocket and dispatches parsed onmessage events only; it does not implement onclose/onerror handling, auto-reconnect, last-sequence tracking, snapshot fetch, or event replay helpers.
The app creates the event WebSocket only inside connect(); it does not listen for WebSocket close/error events and does not resync an active session after a connection interruption.

Each runner records HostEvents with monotonically increasing seq values in an in-memory EventLog. Session snapshots contain the host-materialized timeline and nextSeq, and eventsSince(seq) can replay events greater than seq while the daemon/runner is alive.

The client reducer applies timeline deltas only to existing assistant/thinking items. If a timeline_item or some timeline_delta events are missed over the WebSocket, the active mobile timeline can remain incomplete until a snapshot or replay is applied.

content: Found that host-side event logging and snapshot materialization exist, but the mobile app currently only consumes live WebSocket messages and lacks reconnection/resync logic.
Preparing concise answer describing current behavior and intended recovery path.

Summarized that transient latency is okay if the WebSocket stays open, but an actual disconnect can cause the current client to miss live rendering because it does not auto-reconnect or replay/snapshot yet. Host has seq/event-log/snapshot primitives to add robust catch-up.
